messages:
cs-lead: FYI acme reported mass 503s for embeddings starting ~09:12 PT, spike in errors and latencies. They see ~25-40% errors on the embeddings endpoint.

marta: Ack — I see the same in our SRE dash, worker pool 'hosted-embed-prod' p95 latency doubled, errors map to upstream 503.

oncall-bot: Paging @samir (oncall) — incident auto-detected: hosted-embed-prod error-rate > 20% for 3m.

samir: I'm on it. Can someone paste the last few logs from an affected runner?

emily: grabbing logs now. quick tail:
```
2026-03-17 16:11:58 infer-runner[pid=2345]: kv_prefetch: evicting 0.8GB, trying to allocate 1.2GB
2026-03-17 16:12:01 infer-runner[pid=2345]: cudaError(2): out of memory while allocating buffer for attention_kv
2026-03-17 16:12:03 infer-runner[pid=2345]: segfault at 0x7ffdabc0 (signal 11)
2026-03-17 16:12:04 systemd: infer-runner crashed, respawning
```

ops-jen: that looks like a GPU OOM followed by an illegal memory access. Did we recently flip any quantization/runtime flags?

marta: Yes — we rolled model v3.2 -> v3.2-quantized in canary this morning to hit cost targets. Canary looked fine under low traffic.

samir: If quantized variant uses different kernel paths, fragmentation under high prefetch could trigger OOMs. Need repro plan.

cs-lead: Customer impact: Acme is on Premium; they're seeing failed requests in production. CS on hold, they're asking for ETA.

emily: Repro steps I'm running locally (shortened):
1) send high QPS embedding batch (100 concurrent requests) with long context (3k tokens)
2) observe gpu mem growth + first OOM on prefetched KV
3) within ~10s some runners segfault

samir: Good. Try forcing non-quantized model for that customer via routing to verify hypothesis. Can @marta flip routing for acme to v3.2 non-quantized?

marta: Done — route change pushed (sticky for 10m) for acme -> v3.2. Monitoring now.

oncall-bot: Route update accepted by control-plane, policy id rp-842.

ops-jen: Early data: after routing acme off quantized variant error-rate dropped to ~2% for their API key. Other customers still hit errors (some traffic still on quantized pool).

samir: That strongly implicates quantized runtime path. Next: revert canary -> scale down quantized pool and roll back the autoscaler config that increases prefetch size.

emily: I can push a hotfix to autoscaler config: reduce kv_prefetch_limit from 1.5GB -> 900MB (temporary). Would that reduce OOM pressure?

samir: Yes, do that and spin down any runner pods that already crashed to force fresh allocation paths. Command: `kubectl -n hosted scale deployment/runner-quantized --replicas=0 && sleep 10 && kubectl scale deploy/runner-quantized --replicas=10`

marta: Executed. Also created incident ticket INC-2026-0452 and added acme CS thread.

ops-jen: Observing the fleet: crash rate for runner-quantized decreased after scale bounce and prefetch limit change. Error-rate across hosted-embed-prod fell from 30% -> 6% in 6m.

cs-lead: Good. Customer CS wrote back asking for root cause and remediation plan. Suggest we prepare a short RCA and rollback timeline.

emily: Uploading core dumps and gdb traces to /s3/incidents/INC-2026-0452/ now. Sample gdb bt:
```
#0  0x00007f9a1234 in gpu_mem_copy () from /opt/runtime/lib/libattn.so
#1  0x00007f9a5678 in attn_forward at attn.c:458
#2  0x0000567890 in runner_main
```
Possible null pointer after failed allocation.

samir: Action items:
- short: keep quantized pool scaled down, routing to non-quantized for impacted customers, increase monitoring alerts for quantized OOMs
- mid: revert the canary promotion and pause automated quant-swap rollouts until we have kernel-level validation
- long: reproduce in staging with high prefetch and run under asan-like tooling / collect more mem traces

marta: I've paused the canary promotion and added block in the release pipeline.

oncall-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2 by @samir.

cs-lead: CS has notified Acme that we mitigated customer traffic and will follow up with RCA within 24h. They requested a timeframe for permanent fix.

emily: Will post repro artifacts + a writeup to the incident ticket by EOD. Also adding metric: `runner.quantized.oom_count` to the alert dashboard.

samir: Good work. If anyone notices a reappearance ping me immediately. I'll coordinate the postmortem and include kernel/gpu driver team. :thumbsup:

marta: closing loop here — monitoring stable 15m. Leaving controls in conservative state until postmortem.

cs-lead: Thanks team. I'll update CS thread and log timeline.
